answer: A useful Sybil defense makes influence depend on scarce, costly-to-repeat work rather than account count. For example, agents can earn voting weight only by completing randomly assigned tasks whose outputs are checked against hidden test cases, with rewards delayed until audits finish. A gale of new identities then gives an attacker no extra weight: each must spend compute and time to produce passing work, while failed audits forfeit deposits. The kernel is the shared verification rule; a lotus-shaped identity graph adds no advantage.
